items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: President Carter invited us to play at the Carter Center so we played there.

ctx.x: This has been a wonderful conversation, I’m really glad we could have it. I’m going to wrap up with an observation about your playing and then I’m going to put you on the spot for a moment. I particularly noticed your wonderful ability to play subtone really down at the bottom of the tenor. And then on the other hand when you played your soprano it was like ballsy. Because I hate when the soprano is played like you’re using one lung, that sort of like special — at any rate, I want to know what to wrap up, what do…

Wow that’s definitely putting me on the spot. Well I try — the first thing you hear from a person is their voice, right? I mean so whether you’re talking or singing or almost like — so you know the appealing nature of sounds, so I feel like okay the first thing you have is like the ability hopefully to translate — and I tell this to young musicians, I’ve had students over the years, talking about you are the instrument. Because the saxophone is just a piece of metal. You can put a different mouthpiece and…

sounding thing and I’m playing a wooden mouthpiece so I try to have the like low resonance of — so I don’t know, I mean I do my best to humanize it and, you know, in all of this thing I should just maybe end with saying about this ensemble that I have called the Universal Spirits Ensemble and it’s a group of musicians — it was originally for the idea of the conflict that was happening with the Israeli-Palestinian-Lebanese because I figured okay this is thirty years ago but now the world is just everything is…
